newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's crude ports all reopened - Pemex.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's crude ports all reopened - Pemex.

text.p: Two of Mexico's crude ports reopened Thursday after strong winds forced them shut for three consecutive days, a spokeswoman for state-owned oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said Thursday.
A cold front in the Gulf of Mexico caused crude shipping to be suspended for three days at Pajaritos in Veracruz state and Dos Bocas in Tabasco state.
Pajaritos ships an average 399,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude, while Dos Bocas exports about 440,000 bpd, according to Pemex's latest figures.
The third and largest of Mexico's crude ports, Cayo Arcas in Campeche state, remained open throughout the storms. The port ships an average 611,000 bpd of crude per day.
